In previous meetings, the following agreements were made related to CSI framework: In this contribution, we discuss further details of the CSI framework. The NR CSI reporting framework agreed so far represents an evolution of LTE CSI reporting, allowing a wide variety of use cases, as well as dynamic reuse of CSI-RS resources across multiple users through pooling. The NR framework uses a decoupled approach between the Resource setting and CSI reporting settings, where resource settings can be used for channel as well as interference measurements, allowing for creative use of these components tailored for certain deployments.

In previous meetings, the following agreements were made related to CSI framework: In this contribution, we discuss further details of the CSI framework. The NR CSI reporting framework agreed so far represents an evolution of LTE CSI reporting, allowing a wide variety of use cases, as well as dynamic reuse of CSI-RS resources across multiple users through pooling. The NR framework uses a decoupled approach between the Resource setting and CSI reporting settings, where resource settings can be used for channel as well as interference measurements, allowing for creative use of these components tailored for certain deployments.

CSI-RS has been agreed to be used for at least 3 purposes: for mobility, beam management and CSI acquisition. In principle, it should be the same CSI-RS for different purpose, however, different A.I. has agreed on different design principle on CSI-RS. In this paper, we summarized the agreement mobility, beam management and CSI acquisition A.I. regarding CSI-RS design focusing on the agreements which lead different CSI-RS design.

The current version of the CSI framework has evolved over time in RAN1. The main agreements for CSI framework was achieved in RAN1#87 and RAN1#87AH1 in Spokane.
